title: Claim Conditions by DriveSure Plan — Vehicle Service Contracts
content:
The conditions a repair claim under Vehicle Service Contracts is measured against — the waiting period, authorization before repair, the repair facility, maintenance records and the administrator's decision time — are the same under every DriveSure plan.

## Appendix: claim conditions

| Condition | DriveSure Powertrain | Powertrain Plus | Silver | Gold | Platinum | Exclusionary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting period, calendar days after enrollment before a breakdown is covered | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Waiting period, miles after the odometer at sale before a breakdown is covered | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 |
| Repair facility must obtain authorization before starting a repair | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Maintenance records required when a claim involves a lubricated part | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Longest oil-change interval accepted in maintenance records (miles) | 7500 | 7500 | 7500 | 7500 | 7500 | 7500 |
| Business days within which the administrator authorizes or denies a complete claim | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |

**Where covered repairs may be done (every plan):** any licensed repair facility with ASE-certified technicians.

**Maintenance records.** Where the borrower must show records, they are the manufacturer-recommended maintenance records, and they are measured against the longest accepted oil-change interval of 7500 miles.

## Notes on the figures (hypothetical vehicle)

- With an odometer at sale of 52000 miles, the mileage part of the waiting period runs to 53000 miles (52000 plus 1000).
- Maintenance records showing oil changes 7000 miles apart are within the 7500-mile interval; records showing a gap of 8000 miles between oil changes are not.
